terms.gloss: in the middle; the middle of
evidence: Plaut. Curc. 4.1.14: in forō mediō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says “the middle road” for “the middle of the road”: in mediā viā; the town centre is media urbs (see town centre).

evidence: Liv. 1.57.9: in mediō aedium sedēns (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: As a noun of place it is rare in Cicero (Lewis & Short); the adjective is the usual way.
Greek κέντρον, the fixed point of the compasses: a word of geometry.

terms.gloss: the navel; the very centre of a place
terms.comment: Henna was called the navel of Sicily because it lies in the middle of the island (Cic. Verr. 2.4.106).

phrases.latin: arcum retēnsum posuit in mediā viā
phrases.english: he laid the unstrung bow down in the middle of the road
in the middle is a white honeycomb

phrases.latin: item esse hominēs sub eādem regiōne caelī ūnum oculum in frontis mediō habentēs, quī appellantur Arimaspī
phrases.english: and that under the same part of the sky there are men with one eye in the middle of the forehead, who are called Arimaspians

sources: Lewis & Short: medius · Lewis & Short: medium · Lewis & Short: centrum · Lewis & Short: umbilicus
